drafts.title: $394: AI-built fake stores this Black Friday
drafts.angle: AI can fake a whole store in an afternoon. His own quick check before buying from a store he's never heard of. Fresh vs his earlier scam-text posts: this is fake stores, not texts or voice.
bullets: Norton survey of 1,000 US adults: 16% said they'd been scammed shopping online during the holidays; 88% of those lost money, average $394 (CNBC, Nov 20).
Norton's scam research head says scammers use AI to spin up thousands of fake e-shops with fake product photos and reviews.
FTC data: over 40% of people who lost money to a social media scam said it started with an ad they ordered from (via Guardio).
Tips: skip past sponsored results, search the seller name plus the word scam, type the store address yourself, pay by credit card, never gift card, wire, or crypto.

$394. That's the average hit when people get scammed shopping online over the holidays.

A lot of these start with an ad in your feed. The deal looks too good because it is.

My check before I buy from a store I've never heard of:
1. Search the store name plus the word scam.
2. Type the address myself instead of tapping the ad.
